message:
fix(cobol-gnucobol-benmandrew): start bcrypt batch deadline at job arrival

The bcrypt collector started the batch deadline when a hasher became
free. A password that had already queued behind busy hashers then
waited a further full BC-WAIT-MS window on top of its queue time.

Each queued job now records its arrival time. The deadline is the
arrival time of the head (oldest) job plus BC-WAIT-MS. When no hasher
is idle, the deadline is cleared. A hasher that finishes wakes the
epoll loop, so a stale deadline is not needed, and clearing it avoids
a zero-timeout spin on a deadline that has already passed.

Raise the default BCRYPT_WAIT_MS from 100 to 500 ms. At 48,000 users,
96% of batches fill to four jobs (15% at 100 ms) and the mean wait is
221 ms. Logins are 1 in 900 requests, so p95 and p99 are not at risk.
The README Poisson analysis and table now use the 500 ms window.

Checked with the conformance suite (197/197 pass) and a quick local
loadgen run (3,000 users, think-scale 0.2, dev seed). The run passed
with 0 errors, login p50 357 ms and max 580 ms.
